title: Cross-encoder arbitration matrix and canary rollout plan for multilingual reranker
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our current multilingual reranking route shows variability in quality across locales and tail latency spikes under burst load. We need a principled selection process for cross-encoder variants (tiny/compact/base/large) plus a deterministic canary matrix and rollback criteria that balance MRR/NDCG improvements against p95/p99 latency and per-request cost.

Goals:
- Define an arbitration matrix that maps locale/traffic tier -> preferred cross-encoder variant and fallback variant.
- Create an evaluation harness that computes quality (MRR, NDCG@10, pairwise accuracy) and latency (p50/p95/p99) and cost-per-1000-requests for each candidate on our production-like replay data.
- Produce a staged canary rollout plan (0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 100%) with automatic regression gates and an A/B comparison baseline.
- Implement runtime routing flags and sampling to enable hybrid inference (e.g., cheap candidate generation + expensive cross-encoder rescore for a subsample).

Key success criteria (for go/no-go at each stage):
1) Quality: +3% relative MRR across validated locales OR absolute NDCG@10 uplift >= 0.015 across primary languages.
2) Latency: p95 increase <= 15ms (absolute) on Dedicated and hosted lanes; p99 must remain within SLO budget.
3) Cost: incremental per-1000-request cost delta limited to +25% for routes that see traffic uplift; show cost amortization via sampling/batching for other routes.
4) Regression safety: No locale-level degradation > 2% MRR in APAC/EU/NA.

Planned work items:
- Create candidate matrix: run all cross-encoder variants (quantized FP16/int8 where supported) against a stratified replay (30k queries: 50% NA/30% EU/20% APAC). Capture quality + latency + memory + warm-start KV hit behavior. (owner: Diego)
- Implement micro-benchmark harness in rerank service to measure KV cache priming and per-token kernel selection differences for each variant. (owner: Wei Lin)
- Build canary controller: feature-flag driven traffic percentages, metrics plumbing to Console dashboards, automatic rollback triggers. (owner: Priya Shah)
- Design canary analysis notebook and thresholds (owner: ML-eval team)
- Update SDK and API docs to expose rerank variant hints and per-request sampling header for hybrid flows. (owner: DevEx)

Rollout plan:
- Stage 0 (dry run): offline evaluation & cost model (week 1)
- Stage 1 (0.1%): run for 24h, automated checks for MRR/NDCG and latency tail (week 2)
- Stage 2 (1%): 48h, full regression suite + human review (week 3)
- Stage 3 (10%): 3 days, evaluate cost and slotting under peak traffic windows (week 4)
- Full (100%): contingent on pass criteria and exec approval (week 5)

Rollback criteria (automatic):
- Any locale shows MRR drop > 2.0% relative to baseline for 30m window AND absolute NDCG regression > 0.01
- p95 latency uplift > 25ms sustained for 10m window
- Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline

Acceptance criteria for completion of this ticket:
- Arbitration matrix committed to repo and loaded into routing config with sane defaults
- Canary controller implemented and tested in staging; dashboards updated
- Offline evaluation artifact (notebook + metrics CSV) uploaded to Confluence with reproducible steps
- Runbook documenting rollback steps and postmortem template

Notes on uniqueness and trade-offs:
- We'll adopt hybrid sampling to control cost: only a cached-first lightweight reranker runs at 100% while the expensive cross-encoder is sampled for 10% to validate quality; routing rules will escalate variant for VIP customers.
- For some APAC locales the compact variant + int8 quantization shows similar quality but lower memory; we might adopt locale-specific defaults to preserve latency SLOs.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: model training and full re-embedding of the corpus (that is a separate PM milestone).
